text:
lee: Heads-up: onboarding canary for lark-int4 shows structured-output parse regressions concentrated on very short funcalls (single-field args). Jumped from 0.3% -> 1.8% overnight.

carmen: can you paste a failing example?

lee: sure, small one I pulled out: 
```
int4: {\"tool\":\"set_status\",\"args\":{\"text\":\"can\u2019t do that\"}}
parser: Error: Invalid escape sequence at 16

fp16: {\"tool\":\"set_status\",\"args\":{\"text\":\"can't do that\"}}
```

ankit: hmm the smart-apostrophe is the culprit again. Looks like some subtoken emitted as U+2019.

lee: different pattern from previous: also saw bare backslashes inserted in some samples -> double-escaping. Example: `\\n` inside string produced by int4 but not fp16.

infra-bot: Canary alert: lark-int4 structured_output.parse_fail_rate = 1.8% (baseline=0.3%) on suite/funcall-golden.

carmen: immediate options: 1) strict rollback to fp16 for that canary cohort, 2) post-gen sanitizer that normalizes quotes and collapses duplicate backslashes, 3) adaptive fallback: if parse fails, re-invoke fp16 for that request and compare.

lee: I'm leaning to (3) for Hosted so customer requests degrade gracefully. But (3) doubles cost for those unlucky requests. We need a cheap quickfix too.

ankit: cheap quickfix I prototyped: a tiny normalize step that runs replace(U+2019->U+0027), unescape duplicated backslashes, NFKC normalize, then strict parse. In local bench it recovered ~75% of current failures.

carmen: we must track "repaired_by_normalizer" in telemetry with upstream parse_fail flag preserved (so we can still see raw model regressions). Do not mark repaired as success for gating.

lee: agreed. Also propose we add a gating rule: if parse_fail_rate > 1% on short outputs (<200 chars) AND repaired_by_normalizer < 50% then block canary. Otherwise allow with sanitizer flagged.

qa-bot: Test job queued: lark-int4-normalizer-smoke-171823-1.

ankit: another angle: preprompting. Add a one-line instruction in the system prompt: "Use ASCII single quotes (') for contractions; do not emit smart quotes or control chars." Might reduce the issue with minimal perf impact. Worth A/Bing in canary.

carmen: we should be careful: prompt changes can mask downstream fine-tuning/quantization issues. If we do prompt A/B it must be explicit in telemetry as "prompt-escape-v1".

lee: action list: 
- ankit: land normalizer behind feature-flag in parser + telemetry labels (PR in next 2 hours)
- carmen: implement gating tweak and telemetry dashboards to show raw_fail / repaired_by_normalizer / fallback_fp16 counts
- lee: enable adaptive-fallback for Hosted only, scoped to short outputs and behind rate caps
- qa-bot: run smoke job and post results to thread

infra-bot: Update: lark-int4-normalizer-smoke-171823-1 finished. Repair rate=72%, parse_fail_rate (post-normalizer) = 0.52%. Fallback_fp16_triggers = 0 so far.

carmen: that's promising. Let's ship sanitizer as opt-in to Dedicated and Hosted while we investigate tokenization/quant pairing with the model team.

ankit: I'll also spin up a tokenizer-stability test that forces token-level sampling and logs token boundaries for failed samples; hope to identify subtokens most susceptible to quant noise.

lee: thanks. remind me to add a few contrived golden cases (names with diacritics, contractions, emoji-only messages) to the onboarding suite so we catch regressions earlier.

carmen: +1. Also add a daily diff job comparing int4 vs fp16 on the short-output slice and post a digest to #eng-ml.

lee: cool. I'll follow up with PR link and short demo tomorrow. :slightly_smiling_face:
